references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:41-46|Matthew 22:41-46] where Jesus asks the Pharisees the same question about how the Messiah can be David's son.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:35-37|Mark 12:35-37] where Jesus, in the temple, asks how the scribes can say that the Messiah is David's son.

[ref:Ps 110:1|Psalm 110:1] is the Old Testament passage Jesus quotes in the following verse to show that David himself calls the Messiah "Lord", pointing to the fact that the Messiah is more than just a descendant of David.

[ref:Isa 9:6-7|Isaiah 9:6-7] prophesies about a child who is born and a son who is given, who will sit on David's throne and be called "Mighty God" – a prophecy showing that the Messiah is both a descendant of David and divine.

[ref:Jer 23:5-6|Jeremiah 23:5-6] speaks of a righteous branch whom God will raise up from David's line, who will be called "The Lord our Righteousness" – a union of Davidic lineage and divine identity.
[ref:Rom 1:3-4|Romans 1:3-4] expresses the dual perspective Jesus refers to: He is of David's seed according to the flesh, but appointed Son of God in power – thus both David's son and David's Lord.

[ref:Luke 1:32-33|Luke 1:32-33] where the angel Gabriel announces that Jesus will receive David's throne and be called the Son of the Most High, confirming his identity as both a descendant of David and the Son of God.

[ref:Acts 2:34-36|Acts 2:34-36] where Peter, in his Pentecost sermon, quotes [ref:Ps 110:1|Psalm 110:1] and explains that God has made Jesus – who was crucified – both Lord and Messiah, thus answering the question Jesus asks here.

[ref:Rev 22:16|Revelation 22:16] where Jesus himself says: "I am the root and offspring of David" – he is both David's root (origin/Lord) and David's descendant, thereby resolving the apparent paradox in the question.
